question: The Hathigumpha Inscription was inscribed in which of the following historical regions of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalinga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Hathigumpha Inscription is located in Udayagiri hills near Bhubaneswar in Odisha, which is part of the ancient region of Kalinga.
 
• It was inscribed by King Kharavela, the ruler of the Kalinga kingdom, in the 2nd century BCE.
 
• The inscription is carved in Brahmi script and Prakrit language.
 
• It provides a detailed account of King Kharavela's reign, military conquests, and public works.
 
• The Hathigumpha Inscription is a significant archaeological and historical source for understanding the history of ancient Kalinga and early Indian epigraphy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **King Kharavela:**

 
 
• He was a prominent Jain king of Kalinga who ruled during the 2nd century BCE.
 
• Known for his military campaigns, cultural patronage, and public welfare activities.
 
 
 
• **Udayagiri and Khandagiri Caves:**
 
 
• A complex of rock-cut caves that served as residential retreats for Jain monks.
 
• The Hathigumpha Inscription is located at the entrance of one of these caves.
 
 
 
• **Brahmi Script:**
 
 
• An ancient script used in India, which is the ancestor of many modern Indian scripts.
 
• It was prevalent during the Maurya and Gupta periods.
 
 
 
• **Prakrit Language:**
 
 
• An ancient Indian language used in inscriptions and literature.
 
• It was widely spoken and understood in ancient India, especially in royal inscriptions.
